input.strategy_title: AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement for serving and training
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Two strategic customers are standardizing on AMD Instinct accelerators and need
RHOAI to serve and train on ROCm. Upstream vLLM and PyTorch both publish ROCm
support, but the platform ships only CUDA runtime builds, and we have no
first-hand data on functional or performance parity for our supported model
set. Feature and performance validation requires physical AMD GPU hardware —
none exists in our CI fleet today — and upstream ROCm image cadence is
controlled by AMD and the upstream communities.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware establishes functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for productization. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the models the validation campaign clears. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states supported AMD hardware, driver prerequisites, and the validated model list. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Serving Runtimes
- Training Operator
- Distributed Workloads

## Out of Scope

- Intel Gaudi or other non-AMD accelerator families
- AMD GPU sharing/partitioning support

## Open Questions

1. Hardware access: the validation campaign (HLR-1) needs dedicated AMD
   Instinct nodes — procurement or partner-lab access is unresolved.
2. Upstream ROCm build cadence: whether AMD's runtime image releases align
   with our release trains is outside our control.

# AMD Instinct validation campaign for vLLM serving parity

## Description

This epic delivers the first-hand functional and performance validation of vLLM serving on physical AMD Instinct accelerators, covering the platform's supported model set. It resolves the strategy's central unknown — whether ROCm builds of vLLM reach functional and performance parity with the productized CUDA builds for the models RHOAI supports — and produces the go/no-go scope that determines which models the productized ROCm serving runtime will support. The campaign runs against upstream vLLM ROCm builds on dedicated AMD Instinct hardware; it does not depend on any productized platform artifact.

## Scope

- Secure access to dedicated AMD Instinct nodes (procurement or partner-lab arrangement) — see Risks.
- Define the validation methodology: the supported model set under test, functional pass/fail criteria per model, and performance-parity measurement baselines against the productized CUDA runtime builds.
- Execute the functional validation: serving each supported model on vLLM ROCm builds on the AMD Instinct nodes, including OpenAI-compatible endpoint behavior.
- Execute the performance validation: throughput and latency measurements per model, compared against the CUDA baseline data.
- Produce the campaign report: per-model functional results, per-model performance parity data, and the go/no-go recommendation listing the models cleared for productization.
- Track upstream vLLM/ROCm image releases used during the campaign so results are reproducible.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The campaign report documents, for every model in the supported model set, a functional pass/fail result from serving that model on a vLLM ROCm build on AMD Instinct hardware.
- The campaign report documents, for every functionally passing model, performance measurements (throughput and latency) with the comparison baseline and parity assessment against the CUDA runtime builds.
- The campaign report states a go/no-go recommendation with an explicit list of models cleared for productization.
- Every build tested is identified by a pinned upstream image reference recorded in the report.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)**: A validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware establishes functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for productization. This epic is the full delivery of HLR-1.

## Risks / Notes

- **Hardware access (open question 1)**: dedicated AMD Instinct nodes do not exist in the CI fleet; procurement or partner-lab access is unresolved and controlled by parties outside this strategy. Access being granted is an availability precondition, not an acceptance criterion — the ACs above sit on the report the campaign produces. The epic's work includes driving the access arrangement to completion.
- **Upstream cadence (open question 2)**: upstream ROCm image releases are controlled by AMD and the upstream communities; mid-campaign image updates may force re-runs. Pinned image references in the report mitigate reproducibility risk.
- The go/no-go scope decision may require product-owner sign-off beyond the measured data; the campaign delivers the recommendation, and the sign-off is the gating human step for downstream productization.

# Productize supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime for validated models

## Description

This epic delivers a supported, productized vLLM ROCm serving runtime for the models the AMD Instinct validation campaign clears. It builds a ROCm variant of the vLLM runtime image from the existing midstream vLLM repo, defines the ServingRuntime/ClusterServingRuntime resources that deploy it on AMD GPU nodes, and brings the runtime through the platform's release and support process so it ships per platform version alongside the CUDA builds. The scope of supported models is determined by the campaign's go/no-go outcome; this epic starts once that outcome is known.

## Scope

- Build the vLLM ROCm runtime image variant in the existing midstream vLLM repo, based on the upstream ROCm builds validated by the campaign.
- Define the ServingRuntime (or ClusterServingRuntime) resource that schedules the ROCm runtime on AMD GPU nodes, mirroring the existing CUDA runtime resources.
- Restrict the supported/validated model surface to the models cleared by the validation campaign's go/no-go scope.
- Validate serving through KServe InferenceServices using the ROCm runtime (passive-component validation: KServe itself requires no code change — endpoint readiness and request serving must be demonstrated through the standard InferenceService path).
- Align the release with an upstream ROCm base image that is available and supportable for the target platform version (see Risks).
- Provide rollout/rollback safety: the CUDA runtime builds remain the default; the ROCm runtime is selectable without displacing existing deployments.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A vLLM ROCm runtime image is built from the midstream repo and released with a platform-version-pinned reference.
- A ServingRuntime resource deploying the ROCm image is available and, when selected, serves models on AMD GPU nodes through KServe InferenceServices with endpoints reporting Ready.
- Every model listed as supported by this runtime is on the validated list produced by the AMD Instinct validation campaign, and that mapping is recorded.
- Serving of at least the cleared model set is demonstrated end-to-end on AMD Instinct hardware through the InferenceService path.
- The build pipeline for the ROCm image is green through the Konflux pipeline (this epic does not wait on the pipeline-onboarding work as a dependency; the green pipeline is a completion condition of this epic's release).
- Existing CUDA-based serving runtimes continue to deploy and serve unchanged when the ROCm runtime is introduced (rollback/default-behavior safety).
- The release uses an upstream ROCm base image whose availability aligns with the platform release train, or the misalignment is escalated and recorded with a mitigation.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)**: A supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the models the validation campaign clears. This epic is the full delivery of HLR-2, gated on HLR-1's campaign outcome for its model scope.

## Risks / Notes

- **Upstream ROCm build cadence (open question 2)**: AMD's runtime image release timing is outside our control and may not align with platform release trains; a misalignment is a release-planning escalation, not a code change.
- **Gate**: this epic's model scope is rewritten by the validation campaign's go/no-go outcome — a narrower cleared list narrows the supported model surface; a total no-go would remove the epic.

# Konflux build pipeline for the vLLM ROCm serving runtime image

## Description

This epic onboards the vLLM ROCm runtime image build to Konflux so the new image variant is built, validated, and released through the platform's standard pipeline, like the existing CUDA runtime images. The midstream vLLM repo is already Konflux-onboarded; this epic adds the pipeline/application configuration for the ROCm image variant. This is known-recipe onboarding work that is needed for any go outcome of the validation campaign and proceeds in parallel with the campaign and with the runtime productization work.

## Scope

- Add Konflux application/pipeline configuration for the vLLM ROCm image variant in the already-onboarded midstream vLLM repo.
- Wire the image build, including the ROCm base image inputs, into the existing release automation so the ROCm variant is produced per platform version.
- Ensure pipeline outputs (images, provenance) are visible to the release process used for the serving runtime.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A Konflux pipeline builds the vLLM ROCm image variant from the midstream repo and completes green.
- The pipeline is wired into the release automation so the ROCm image variant is produced as part of a platform version build.
- The pipeline run records the ROCm base image inputs used for the build.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)** (enabling): A supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the cleared models — this epic provides the build/release infrastructure that productization requires. It carries no DAG dependency on the productization work: the two run in parallel, with the pipeline-green condition expressed as an acceptance criterion on the productization epic.

## Risks / Notes

- The ROCm base image inputs track AMD's upstream release cadence (open question 2); the pipeline must tolerate base-image updates between platform versions.

# PyTorch ROCm training support for PyTorchJob single- and multi-GPU jobs

## Description

This epic delivers PyTorch training on ROCm for jobs run through the Training Operator: ROCm-enabled PyTorch training runtime images and the PyTorchJob configuration needed to run single-GPU and multi-GPU (including multi-node) training jobs on AMD Instinct nodes. It provides the training half of the AMD enablement independent of the serving validation outcome — training support proceeds on the strength of upstream PyTorch ROCm support and is validated directly on the hardware.

## Scope

- Build/enable the ROCm variant of the PyTorch training runtime image used by PyTorchJob workers.
- Verify PyTorchJob single-GPU and multi-GPU job topologies run on AMD Instinct nodes with the ROCm training runtime.
- Verify multi-node jobs are admitted and run through the platform's workload queueing when enabled (gang admission of the job's pods).
- Validate functional training correctness (loss convergence / job completion) for representative training workloads on ROCm.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A PyTorchJob using the ROCm training runtime completes successfully on AMD Instinct hardware in single-GPU configuration.
- A PyTorchJob using the ROCm training runtime completes successfully in multi-GPU configuration on AMD Instinct hardware.
- A multi-node PyTorchJob is admitted through a Kueue queue configured for the `amd.com/gpu` resource and runs to completion (end-to-end admission check; the quota configuration itself is delivered by the Distributed Workloads quota-handling work and consumed here as a configuration reference).
- Job results demonstrate training correctness (jobs complete without ROCm-related failures) for the tested workloads.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P1)**: PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling. This epic delivers the training-runtime and PyTorchJob half of HLR-3; the quota-handling half is delivered by the Distributed Workloads epic.

## Risks / Notes

- Validation requires access to dedicated AMD Instinct nodes — the same availability precondition as the serving validation campaign (procurement/partner lab, unresolved). Job validation is scheduled around whatever access window is secured.
- Upstream PyTorch/ROCm release cadence (open question 2) may limit which ROCm versions can be validated per platform release.
- The mechanism that exposes the `amd.com/gpu` resource on nodes (AMD GPU device plugin/operator) is not part of the platform inventory and is not addressed by the strategy; this epic assumes it is present on the target clusters. Flagged in the decomposition summary for human verification.

# Kueue quota handling for the amd.com/gpu resource

## Description

This epic delivers quota handling for the `amd.com/gpu` resource in the platform's Kueue-based queueing layer, so workloads requesting AMD GPUs are accounted, quota-gated, and admitted with the same all-or-nothing semantics as NVIDIA GPU workloads. It covers the resource-flavor and cluster-queue configuration surface in the Distributed Workloads stack that makes `amd.com/gpu` a quota-managed resource.

## Scope

- Define the ResourceFlavor covering nodes that expose the `amd.com/gpu` resource.
- Provide the ClusterQueue/LocalQueue configuration pattern for `amd.com/gpu` quota, mirroring the existing NVIDIA GPU quota handling.
- Verify quota accounting: workloads requesting `amd.com/gpu` are admitted only when quota is available, and pending/admitted accounting is correct.
- Verify gang semantics: multi-pod workloads requesting `amd.com/gpu` are admitted all-or-nothing (waitForPodsReady behavior).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A workload requesting `amd.com/gpu` is admitted by a ClusterQueue configured with the AMD resource flavor when quota is available, and remains pending when it is not.
- Quota accounting for `amd.com/gpu` matches admitted usage (no over-admission beyond configured quota).
- A multi-pod workload requesting `amd.com/gpu` is admitted all-or-nothing — partial pod sets are not scheduled when full quota is unavailable.
- The configuration is documented sufficiently for cluster administrators to deploy AMD GPU quota for their queues.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P1)**: PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling. This epic delivers the amd.com/gpu quota-handling half of HLR-3; the training-runtime half is delivered by the Training Operator epic. The two run in parallel — training jobs consume the quota configuration as a configuration reference (acceptance-criterion gate), not as a build dependency.

## Risks / Notes

- The `amd.com/gpu` resource must be exposed on nodes by an AMD GPU device plugin/operator that is not in the platform inventory and is not addressed by the strategy; this epic configures quota against the resource name and assumes exposure exists on target clusters. Flagged in the decomposition summary for human verification — if the exposure mechanism must be productized, an additional epic is needed.

# Document AMD hardware support, driver prerequisites, and validated models

## Description

This epic delivers the customer-facing documentation for AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement: the supported AMD hardware, the driver prerequisites for running serving and training workloads on AMD Instinct accelerators, and the validated model list produced by the validation campaign. It is authored through the Red Hat docs content process once the implementation work it describes is final.

## Scope

Content outline:

- Supported AMD hardware: the AMD Instinct accelerators on which serving and training are supported.
- Driver and cluster prerequisites: AMD driver versions and node requirements, including how the `amd.com/gpu` resource must be exposed on nodes.
- Serving on ROCm: how to deploy the vLLM ROCm serving runtime for the validated models, including model-scope limitations from the validation campaign.
- Training on ROCm: how to run single- and multi-GPU PyTorchJob training on AMD nodes, including Kueue quota configuration for `amd.com/gpu`.
- The validated model list: models cleared by the validation campaign, with the functional/performance parity findings summarized.
- Support boundaries: what is unsupported (GPU sharing/partitioning, non-AMD accelerator families per the strategy's out-of-scope list).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation states the supported AMD Instinct hardware and the driver prerequisites for serving and training.
- Published documentation states the validated model list, matching the go/no-go scope produced by the validation campaign.
